\subsection{Fresh clone-controlled evidence on MATH-500 (WP-1R/WP-2R)}
\label{sec:wp1r}

The archived studies lack matched repeats and a same-code control, so they
cannot separate stable complementarity from one-run sampling luck. A fresh
pre-registered collection (frozen 2026-09-15; Appendix~\ref{app:wp1r})
executes a frozen eight-harness panel plus \bare{} on the 400 MATH-500
eval tasks for three independent repeats, plus nine equal-budget
same-code \bare{} clone slots --- the repeated-sampling baseline of
\S\ref{related:diversity}.

C-rank is \textsc{\WpCrankState}; C-comp is \textsc{\WpCcompState}.
The frozen A8.6 procedure selects the best member on repeat 1 and scores
its held-out advantage over \bare{} on repeats 2--3: $\WpAReal$\,pp (real)
versus $\WpAClone$\,pp (clones), paired $D=\WpADiff$\,pp on
\WpANtasksPaired{} shared complete tasks (95\% CI $\WpADiffCI$;
$p=\WpAPerm$); both sensitivity branches agree ($D=\WpImputedD$ and
$\WpConflictD$\,pp). The frozen coverage gate makes the verdict
\textsc{\WpAState}: no advantage over equal-budget same-code sampling.
The acquisition consumed \WpLogicalCalls{} logical calls (\WpCostCny{}
CNY ceiling) and is hash-sealed.

\paragraph{Selector utility (E3).} The frozen pre-execution policy
$\pi_Z$ abstains to \bare{} on every eval task (no member clears the
frozen 0.15 confidence margin) and so ties both dev-fixed and \bare{} at
\WpBareAcc\%; it realizes no selection gain (paired
$\WpPiZDiff$\,pp, CI $\WpPiZDiffCI$), while a pre-fixed random member is
materially worse ($\WpRandomDiff$\,pp, CI $\WpRandomCI$;
Table~\ref{tab:wp1r-policy}). Class D
therefore yields no evidence of usable pre-execution selectability on
this panel, and the $b{=}3$ budgeted utility $U_b$ (Class E) is likewise
zero for all frozen policies.

and v1.2 (operational test specification) preceded any confirmatory
outcome; v1.3 (attempt ceiling 45{,}000$\to$60{,}000, matching the task

mid-collection for throughput and are disclosed as condition-relevant
history) fixes: the estimands E1--E4 of
\S\ref{sec:wp1r}; the panel draw (eligibility by frozen repeat-0 mean
logical calls ${\leq}3.05$ --- a budget-feasibility filter disclosed as
biasing the panel toward low-call mechanisms, not a uniform sample of the
35 generated members; then a salted-hash draw, one stratum seat per builder
plus two at-large seats, salt \texttt{wp1r-panel-v1-20260915}, recorded in
\texttt{WP1R\_PANEL\_DRAW.json}); $R{=}3$ fresh repeats per arm; the
nine-slot same-code clone arm (\texttt{clone-c1..c9}, byte-identical
\bare{} source) as the exchangeable null; the A8.6 discovery/validation
procedure (discovery repeat 1, validation repeats 2--3, $\delta{=}1.0$\,pp,
10{,}000 permutations, 10{,}000 task bootstrap draws, seed 20260915); the
paired difference and its CI use only the task intersection complete in
both arms; a coverage gate degrades the main verdict to INSUFFICIENT when
either arm excludes more than 10\% of tasks, with two frozen sensitivity
branches (within-task repeat-mean imputation, and exclusion of
doubly-executed conflict cells); and
the acceptance rule that any of SUPPORTED / REFUTED / INSUFFICIENT
terminates the study without re-running or re-sampling. The 400 eval and
100 dev tasks are the frozen MATH-500 split (SHA256 recorded); eval tasks
were analyzed before in the one-run mini-audit, so results are labeled
retrospective-task/prospective-execution, not unseen-task validation.

\paragraph{Execution record and continuation merge.} Collection ran
2026-09-15 through 2026-09-19 under a 60{,}000-attempt global budget with

clone arm across two; each continuation re-binds the identical frozen
solver condition (verified field-by-field at merge). The merge rule is
deterministic: a completed observation beats an \texttt{unknown\_remote}
marker; among completed records of the same cell the earliest ledger wins.
Across the real arm's
\WpRowsRead{} rows it collapsed \WpMigrationCopies{} migration
copies, preferred a completed record over an unknown-remote marker

\WpUnknownCarried{} cells remain
\texttt{unknown\_remote} across all ledgers and stay NaN in the outcome

the frozen rules. The merged arms are hash-sealed

the real arm across continuations (concurrency 2/2/6); each seal records

fields (acquisition id) while this appendix discloses the concurrency and
amendment history. The analysis code and its unit tests are in
\texttt{experiment/revision/wp1r\_analysis.py}.

experiment-run $>$ harness-execution $>$ logical-call $>$ provider-attempt;
migration copies are excluded from the totals (distinct re-executions count
individually). Totals: \WpLogicalCalls{} logical calls, \WpHttpAttempts{}
provider attempts, \WpTotalTokens{} known tokens, conservative cost ceiling
\WpCostCny{} CNY at the frozen break-even price of 33.3 CNY per 1M tokens
(pricing not independently verifiable; reported as token counts times the
frozen price, never as billed amounts).

\paragraph{Selector spec (E3).} $\pi_Z$ is multinomial logistic regression
over TF-IDF question features (max 300) and per-member dev accuracies
computed within training folds only; 5-fold task-level CV on the 100 dev
tasks with same-task repeats never split across folds; fold-model
averaging; ties broken by member id; abstain to \bare{} when the top-2
probability gap is below 0.15. Repeat aggregation uses the
available-repeat mean per member--task (same-task repeats stay in one
fold); the final-ledger unknown/failed counts are reconciled against the
merged-matrix NaN cells in the repository checkpoint. Comparators:
\bare{}, dev-fixed, pre-fixed
random member (seeded), M1b (dev-fixed with bare fallback on missing
cells). $E_1$ (budget by construction) is not applicable because panel
members make more than one call; $E_b$ with $b{=}3$ calls per task is
reported as a separately named estimand. Leakage controls: no answer,
correctness, eval-derived difficulty, post-execution trace, or judge
feature is used.

"""Render WP-1R/WP-2R analysis JSONs into LaTeX macros and a results table.

Reads artifacts/wp1r_20260915/analysis_report.json and
artifacts/wp1r_20260915/wp2r_selector_report.json and writes
paper/latex/wp1r_numbers.tex (\\newcommand macros) and
paper/latex/wp1r_policy_table.tex.  Every number in the WP-1R paper section
comes from this file; no hand-copied values.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WP1R = ROOT / 'artifacts/wp1r_20260915'
TEX = ROOT / 'paper' / 'latex'


def pp(x, digits=2):
    """Format a probability as percentage points with fixed digits."""
    return f'{100 * x:.{digits}f}'


def macro(name, value):
    return f'\\newcommand{{\\{name}}}{{{value}}}'


def policy_table(sel):
    acc = sel['accuracy']
    rows = []
    for name, label in [('bare', r'\bare{} (fixed)'),
                        ('dev_fixed', 'dev-fixed'),
                        ('random_fixed', 'random (pre-fixed)'),
                        ('M1b', 'M1b (dev-fixed + bare fallback)'),
                        ('pi_Z', r'$\pi_Z$ (frozen selector)')]:
        a = acc[name]
        row = f"{label} & {pp(a['accuracy'])}"
        if 'paired_vs_dev_fixed' in a:
            p = a['paired_vs_dev_fixed']
            row += (f" & {pp(p['mean'])} "
                    f"[{pp(p['ci95'][0])}, {pp(p['ci95'][1])}]")
        else:
            row += ' & ---'
        rows.append(row + r' \\')
    return '\n'.join([
        r'\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}',
        r'\toprule',
        r'Policy & Eval acc.\ (\%) & $\Delta$ vs dev-fixed (pp) [95\% CI] \\',
        r'\midrule',
        *rows,
        r'\bottomrule',
        r'\end{tabular}',
    ]) + '\n'


def main():
    report = json.loads((WP1R / 'analysis_report.json')
                        .read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    sel_path = WP1R / 'wp2r_selector_report.json'
    sel = json.loads(sel_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')) \
        if sel_path.exists() else None
    lines = ['% Auto-generated by experiment/revision/wp1r_render.py.',
             '% Do not edit by hand; regenerate after re-running the analysis.']

    a86 = report['E2_A86_clone_null']
    lines += [
        macro('WpAReal', pp(a86['A_real'])),
        macro('WpAClone', pp(a86['A_clone_obs'])),
        macro('WpADiff', pp(a86['D'])),
        macro('WpADiffCI', f"[{pp(a86['D_ci95'][0])}, {pp(a86['D_ci95'][1])}]"),
        macro('WpAPerm', f"{a86['p_perm']:.4f}".lstrip('0')),
        macro('WpAState', a86['state'].replace('_', r'\_')),
        macro('WpANtasksReal', a86['n_tasks_real']),
        macro('WpANtasksClone', a86['n_tasks_clone']),
        macro('WpANtasksPaired', a86['n_tasks_paired']),
        macro('WpExclReal', f"{100 * a86['excluded_frac_real']:.1f}"),
        macro('WpExclClone', f"{100 * a86['excluded_frac_clone']:.1f}"),
        macro('WpImputedD', pp(a86['sensitivity_imputed']['D'])),
        macro('WpImputedNPaired', a86['sensitivity_imputed']['n_tasks_paired']),
    ]
    conflict = report.get('E2_sensitivity_double_executed_conflicts')
    if conflict is not None:
        lines += [
            macro('WpConflictD', pp(conflict['D'])),
            macro('WpConflictCI',
                  f"[{pp(conflict['D_ci95'][0])}, {pp(conflict['D_ci95'][1])}]"),
            macro('WpConflictNExcluded', conflict['n_cells_excluded']),
        ]
    else:
        lines += [macro('WpConflictD', r'\text{---}'),
                  macro('WpConflictCI', r'\text{---}'),
                  macro('WpConflictNExcluded', 0)]

    s3 = report['E1_C-rank_E2_C-comp']
    lines += [
        macro('WpCrankState', s3['stable_ranking']['state'].replace('_', r'\_')),
        macro('WpCcompState', s3['stable_complementarity']['state'].replace('_', r'\_')),
    ]
    sc = s3['stable_complementarity']
    if sc.get('H_stable') is not None:
        lines += [macro('WpHstable', pp(sc['H_stable'])),
                  macro('WpHstableCI',
                        f"[{pp(sc['H_ci95'][0])}, {pp(sc['H_ci95'][1])}]")]
    else:
        lines += [macro('WpHstable', r'\text{abstained}'),
                  macro('WpHstableCI', r'\text{---}')]

    dedup = report['dedup_eval_real']
    lines += [
        macro('WpRowsRead', f"{dedup['rows_read']:,}"),
        macro('WpMigrationCopies', f"{dedup['identical_copies']:,}"),
        macro('WpDoubleExec', len(dedup['both_completed_differ'])),
        macro('WpUnknownCarried', dedup['unknown_carried']),
        macro('WpCompletedBeatsUnknown', dedup['completed_beats_unknown']),
        macro('WpUnknownThenCompleted', dedup['unknown_then_completed']),
    ]
    dedup_c = report.get('dedup_eval_clone')
    if dedup_c:
        lines += [macro('WpCloneRowsRead', f"{dedup_c['rows_read']:,}"),
                  macro('WpCloneMigrationCopies',
                        f"{dedup_c['identical_copies']:,}"),
                  macro('WpCloneUnique', f"{dedup_c['unique_keys']:,}"),
                  macro('WpCloneConflicts', len(dedup_c['both_completed_differ']))]
    else:
        lines += [macro('WpCloneRowsRead', r'\text{---}'),
                  macro('WpCloneMigrationCopies', r'\text{---}'),
                  macro('WpCloneUnique', r'\text{---}'),
                  macro('WpCloneConflicts', r'\text{---}')]

    e4 = report['E4_accounting']['_total']
    lines += [
        macro('WpLogicalCalls', f"{e4['logical_calls']:,}"),
        macro('WpHttpAttempts', f"{e4['http_attempts']:,}"),
        macro('WpTotalTokens', f"{e4['known_total_tokens'] / 1e6:.1f}\\,M"),
        macro('WpCostCny', f"{e4['conservative_cost_ceiling_cny']:,}"),
    ]

    if sel is not None:
        acc = sel['accuracy']
        summ = sel['summary']
        lines += [
            macro('WpDevFixedMember', summ['dev_fixed_member'].replace('_', r'\_')),
            macro('WpAbstainRate', pp(summ['abstain_rate_pi_Z'])),
            macro('WpPiZAcc', pp(acc['pi_Z']['accuracy'])),
            macro('WpDevFixedAcc', pp(acc['dev_fixed']['accuracy'])),
            macro('WpBareAcc', pp(acc['bare']['accuracy'])),
            macro('WpPiZDiff', pp(acc['pi_Z']['paired_vs_dev_fixed']['mean'])),
            macro('WpPiZDiffCI',
                  f"[{pp(acc['pi_Z']['paired_vs_dev_fixed']['ci95'][0])}, "
                  f"{pp(acc['pi_Z']['paired_vs_dev_fixed']['ci95'][1])}]"),
            macro('WpRandomDiff', pp(acc['random_fixed']['paired_vs_dev_fixed']['mean'])),
            macro('WpRandomCI',
                  f"[{pp(acc['random_fixed']['paired_vs_dev_fixed']['ci95'][0])}, "
                  f"{pp(acc['random_fixed']['paired_vs_dev_fixed']['ci95'][1])}]"),
        ]
        (TEX / 'wp1r_policy_table.tex').write_text(
            policy_table(sel), encoding='utf-8')
    else:
        for name in ('WpDevFixedMember', 'WpAbstainRate', 'WpPiZAcc',
                     'WpDevFixedAcc', 'WpBareAcc', 'WpPiZDiff'):
            lines.append(macro(name, r'\text{---}'))
        lines.append(macro('WpPiZDiffCI', r'\text{---}'))
        lines.append(macro('WpRandomDiff', r'\text{---}'))
        lines.append(macro('WpRandomCI', r'\text{---}'))

    (TEX / 'wp1r_numbers.tex').write_text('\n'.join(lines) + '\n',
                                         encoding='utf-8')
    print('wrote', TEX / 'wp1r_numbers.tex',
          'and wp1r_policy_table.tex' if sel else '(selector report pending)')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

\section{WP-1R/WP-2R Fresh Collection: Protocol and Execution Record}
\label{app:wp1r}

\paragraph{Frozen protocol.} The acquisition protocol
(\texttt{review-stage/REAL\_EVIDENCE\_PROTOCOL\_V1.md}, v1.0 frozen
2026-09-15, with dated amendments: v1.1 (statistical and budget fixes)
and v1.2 (operational test specification) preceded any confirmatory
outcome; v1.3 (attempt ceiling 45{,}000$\to$60{,}000, matching the task
authorization) and the concurrency amendment (2$\to$6) were made
mid-collection for throughput and are disclosed as condition-relevant
history) fixes: the estimands E1--E4 of
\S\ref{sec:wp1r}; the panel draw (eligibility by frozen repeat-0 mean
logical calls ${\leq}3.05$ --- a budget-feasibility filter disclosed as
biasing the panel toward low-call mechanisms, not a uniform sample of the
35 generated members; then a salted-hash draw, one stratum seat per builder
plus two at-large seats, salt \texttt{wp1r-panel-v1-20260915}, recorded in
\texttt{WP1R\_PANEL\_DRAW.json}); $R{=}3$ fresh repeats per arm; the
nine-slot same-code clone arm (\texttt{clone-c1..c9}, byte-identical
\bare{} source) as the exchangeable null; the A8.6 discovery/validation
procedure (discovery repeat 1, validation repeats 2--3, $\delta{=}1.0$\,pp,
10{,}000 permutations, 10{,}000 task bootstrap draws, seed 20260915); the
paired difference and its CI use only the task intersection complete in
both arms; a coverage gate degrades the main verdict to INSUFFICIENT when
either arm excludes more than 10\% of tasks, with two frozen sensitivity
branches (within-task repeat-mean imputation, and exclusion of
doubly-executed conflict cells); and
the acceptance rule that any of SUPPORTED / REFUTED / INSUFFICIENT
terminates the study without re-running or re-sampling. The 400 eval and
100 dev tasks are the frozen MATH-500 split (SHA256 recorded); eval tasks
were analyzed before in the one-run mini-audit, so results are labeled
retrospective-task/prospective-execution, not unseen-task validation.

\paragraph{Execution record and continuation merge.} Collection ran
2026-09-15 through 2026-09-19 under a 60{,}000-attempt global budget with
per-cell atomic reservation. Two provider-timeout stops (2026-09-17,
2026-09-18) split the real arm across three continuation ledgers and the
clone arm across two; each continuation re-binds the identical frozen
solver condition (verified field-by-field at merge). The merge rule is
deterministic: a completed observation beats an \texttt{unknown\_remote}
marker; among completed records of the same cell the earliest ledger wins.
Across the real arm's
\WpRowsRead{} rows it collapsed \WpMigrationCopies{} migration
copies, preferred a completed record over an unknown-remote marker
\WpCompletedBeatsUnknown{} times, completed an earlier unknown marker
\WpUnknownThenCompleted{} times, and found \WpDoubleExec{} cells with two
completed but disagreeing executions (first-completed retained; a frozen
sensitivity branch excludes them instead). The clone arm's
\WpCloneRowsRead{} rows collapsed to 10{,}800 unique cells
(\WpCloneMigrationCopies{} copies, zero conflicts).
\WpUnknownCarried{} cells remain
\texttt{unknown\_remote} across all ledgers and stay NaN in the outcome
matrices --- never imputed --- so classes requiring those cells abstain by
the frozen rules. The merged arms are hash-sealed
(\texttt{SEALED\_eval\_real.json}, \texttt{SEALED\_eval\_clone.json},
\texttt{SEALED\_dev\_real.json}). Three collector source versions served
the real arm across continuations (concurrency 2/2/6); each seal records
the arm's bound collector hash, and the identity gates exclude run-identity
fields (acquisition id) while this appendix discloses the concurrency and
amendment history. The analysis code and its unit tests are in
\texttt{experiment/revision/wp1r\_analysis.py}.

\paragraph{Accounting (E4).} Per-request accounting layers
experiment-run $>$ harness-execution $>$ logical-call $>$ provider-attempt;
migration copies are excluded from the totals (distinct re-executions count
individually). Totals: \WpLogicalCalls{} logical calls, \WpHttpAttempts{}
provider attempts, \WpTotalTokens{} known tokens, conservative cost ceiling
\WpCostCny{} CNY at the frozen break-even price of 33.3 CNY per 1M tokens
(pricing not independently verifiable; reported as token counts times the
frozen price, never as billed amounts).

\paragraph{Selector spec (E3).} $\pi_Z$ is multinomial logistic regression
over TF-IDF question features (max 300) and per-member dev accuracies
computed within training folds only; 5-fold task-level CV on the 100 dev
tasks with same-task repeats never split across folds; fold-model
averaging; ties broken by member id; abstain to \bare{} when the top-2
probability gap is below 0.15. Repeat aggregation uses the
available-repeat mean per member--task (same-task repeats stay in one
fold); the final-ledger unknown/failed counts are reconciled against the
merged-matrix NaN cells in the repository checkpoint. Comparators:
\bare{}, dev-fixed, pre-fixed
random member (seeded), M1b (dev-fixed with bare fallback on missing
cells). $E_1$ (budget by construction) is not applicable because panel
members make more than one call; $E_b$ with $b{=}3$ calls per task is
reported as a separately named estimand. Leakage controls: no answer,
correctness, eval-derived difficulty, post-execution trace, or judge
feature is used.

011  Automatically generated LLM harnesses offer a rich design space, but their

012  source-code, execution, and outcome diversity must be measured separately. On

013  BIRD text-to-SQL, trace inspection distinguishes absent, untriggered, and broken

014  mechanisms, and free generation yields 8.6 pp of observed oracle headroom across

018  separately reported claim classes, checked by ordering-invariance, dominance-

020  cation claims. On the archived factorial study the combined screening intervention

021  estimates -0.16 pp (95% CI [-0.83, +0.87]), supporting the measurement con-

022  tribution rather than intervention superiority. A fresh pre-registered MATH-500

023  collection supplies the decisive equal-budget control: an eight-harness panel and

024  nine same-code clone slots, each run for three independent repeats. The panel

025  shows stable member ranking, but stable complementarity is not established and

026  its discovery-selected advantage is indistinguishable from same-code repeated ex-

027  ecution. The framework turns apparent diversity into auditable evidence and iden-

028  tifies the controls required before any deployment claim.

030 1 INTRODUCTION

031

032 An LLM harness is the program of prompts, tools, and control flow that wraps a frozen model.
033 Automatically generating many such programs creates an evaluation problem: what evidence shows

034 that a new program provides a new capability? Different source code may execute the same path;

035 different paths may produce the same answer; different answers on one run may reflect execution
036 randomness rather than a repeatable advantage.

037 We study this problem on BIRD text-to-SQL (Li et al., 2023). In a Phase-I discovery population, 21
038 of 66 generated-candidate pairs had identical correctness vectors. Including the react harness (Yao
039 et al., 2023), shipped with TTHE (Nie et al., 2026), and the bare baseline gives 36 identical pairs

040 out of 91. Pairwise code similarity had no observed rank association with outcome disagreement

041 ( = -0.01). Trace inspection found three distinct situations: claimed mechanisms absent from
042 control flow, mechanisms present but untriggered on the inspected tasks, and broken multi-turn
043 implementations. These observations motivate an audit of the measurement process; they do not
044 establish that generated harnesses generally collapse.

045 A subsequent pre-specified factorial study crossed strategy forcing and conformance gating over six

046 builders and three seeds. Its primary evaluation used 1,169 questions from nine databases outside

047 protocol development, with one disclosed 18-item smoke-test exception. Under this revised setting,
048 free ungated generation already produced 8.6 pp observed oracle headroom. The Phase-I pattern
049 therefore did not recur, but changes in generation, judge, data, and execution prevent attribution to
050 any one protocol component without a controlled bridge.

051 The original gate also changes the admissible strategy space: two allowed single-call prompt trans-

052 formations cannot pass its mechanism check. Consequently, the intervention combines mechanism

053 screening with verification. We preserve that experiment and report a versioned post-review reanal-
          ysis rather than treating it as a repaired-gate trial. The primary contrast remains -0.16 pp (95%

057 Our contribution at this stage is an empirical account of three measurement boundaries, plus a vali-
058 dated diagnostic that operationalizes them:

059  1. Code, trace, and outcome diversity differ. Discovery examples show why an inactive

060         branch and a missing mechanism require different tests.

061  2. Admission and inference define the comparison. A factorial study and an explicit cor-

062         rection of its data and statistical chain show which intervention was actually evaluated and

063         what its estimate supports.

064  3. Observed oracle value is not stable or usable value. Repeat instability and ex-

065         ploratory selection results motivate separate reporting of oracle accuracy, best-fixed ac-

066         curacy, repeated-run advantages, and realized selector performance.

067  4. A validated diagnostic separates the claim classes. An offline procedure evaluates mea-

068         surement sufficiency, single-shot coverage, stable ranking, stable complementarity, pre-

069         execution selectability, and budgeted utility as separate claims with explicit states, identity

070         gates, and invariant-tested, hash-bound validation (�6); on our archives it either abstains

071         by frozen rules or corrects traceable errors, including one of our own earlier verification

072         claims.

073 The decisive question is whether a real harness population outperforms an equal-budget population
074 of independent executions of the same code, with advantages that survive independent repeats. A
075 fresh pre-registered MATH-500 collection supplies exactly this control (�5.4): it finds stable mem-
076 ber ranking but no stable complementarity beyond same-code repeated execution. Stable comple-

\begin{abstract}
Automatically generated LLM harnesses offer a rich design space, but their
source-code, execution, and outcome diversity must be measured separately.
On BIRD text-to-SQL, trace inspection distinguishes absent, untriggered,
and broken mechanisms, and free generation yields 8.6\,pp of observed
oracle headroom across 1{,}169 questions; a one-seed MATH-500 probe
shows 10.6\% outcome disagreement and 4.75\,pp headroom. We formalize
one-run oracle gains, stable ranking, stable complementarity,
pre-execution selectability, and budgeted utility as five separately
reported claim classes, checked by ordering-invariance,
dominance-versus-complementarity, cloned-repeat, and condition-mixing
controls with hash-bound challenge re-execution; the procedure also
corrects one of our earlier verification claims. On the archived
factorial study the combined screening intervention estimates
$\RevisionPrimaryDelta$\,pp (95\% CI $\RevisionPrimaryCI$), supporting
the measurement contribution rather than intervention superiority. A
fresh pre-registered MATH-500 collection supplies the decisive
equal-budget control: an eight-harness panel and nine same-code clone
slots, each run for three independent repeats. The panel shows stable
member ranking, but stable complementarity is not established and its
discovery-selected advantage is indistinguishable from same-code
repeated execution. The framework turns apparent diversity into
auditable evidence and identifies the controls required before any
deployment claim.
\end{abstract}

\subsection{Fresh clone-controlled evidence on MATH-500 (WP-1R/WP-2R)}
\label{sec:wp1r}

The archived studies lack matched repeats and a same-code control, so they
cannot separate stable complementarity from one-run sampling luck. A fresh
pre-registered collection (frozen 2026-09-15; Appendix~\ref{app:wp1r})
executes a frozen eight-harness panel plus \bare{} on the 400 MATH-500
eval tasks for three independent repeats, plus nine equal-budget
same-code \bare{} clone slots --- the repeated-sampling baseline of
\S\ref{related:diversity}.

C-rank is \textsc{\WpCrankState}; C-comp is \textsc{\WpCcompState}.
The frozen A8.6 procedure selects the best member on repeat 1 and scores
its held-out advantage over \bare{} on repeats 2--3: $\WpAReal$\,pp (real)
versus $\WpAClone$\,pp (clones), paired $D=\WpADiff$\,pp on
\WpANtasksPaired{} shared complete tasks (95\% CI $\WpADiffCI$;
$p=\WpAPerm$); both sensitivity branches agree ($D=\WpImputedD$ and
$\WpConflictD$\,pp). The frozen coverage gate makes the verdict
\textsc{\WpAState}: no advantage over equal-budget same-code sampling.
The acquisition consumed \WpLogicalCalls{} logical calls (\WpCostCny{}
CNY ceiling) and is hash-sealed.

\paragraph{Selector utility (E3).} The frozen pre-execution policy
$\pi_Z$ abstains to \bare{} on every eval task (no member clears the
frozen 0.15 confidence margin) and so ties both dev-fixed and \bare{} at
\WpBareAcc\%; it realizes no selection gain (paired
$\WpPiZDiff$\,pp, CI $\WpPiZDiffCI$), while a pre-fixed random member is
materially worse ($-10.12$\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:wp1r-policy}). Class D
therefore yields no evidence of usable pre-execution selectability on
this panel, and the $b{=}3$ budgeted utility $U_b$ (Class E) is likewise
zero for all frozen policies.

retrospective-task/prospective-execution, not unseen-task validation.

\paragraph{Execution record and continuation merge.} Collection ran
2026-09-15 through 2026-09-19 under a 60{,}000-attempt global budget with
per-cell atomic reservation. Two provider-timeout stops (2026-09-17,
2026-09-18) split the real arm across three continuation ledgers and the
clone arm across two; each continuation re-binds the identical frozen
solver condition (verified field-by-field at merge). The merge rule is
deterministic: a completed observation beats an \texttt{unknown\_remote}
marker; among completed records of the same cell the earliest ledger wins.
Across the real arm's
\WpRowsRead{} rows it collapsed \WpMigrationCopies{} migration
copies, preferred a completed record over an unknown-remote marker
\WpCompletedBeatsUnknown{} times, completed an earlier unknown marker
\WpUnknownThenCompleted{} times, and found \WpDoubleExec{} cells with two
completed but disagreeing executions (first-completed retained; a frozen
sensitivity branch excludes them instead). The clone arm's
\WpCloneRowsRead{} rows collapsed to 10{,}800 unique cells
(\WpCloneMigrationCopies{} copies, zero conflicts).
\WpUnknownCarried{} cells remain
\texttt{unknown\_remote} across all ledgers and stay NaN in the outcome
matrices --- never imputed --- so classes requiring those cells abstain by
the frozen rules. The merged arms are hash-sealed
(\texttt{SEALED\_eval\_real.json}, \texttt{SEALED\_eval\_clone.json},
\texttt{SEALED\_dev\_real.json}). Three collector source versions served
the real arm across continuations (concurrency 2/2/6); each seal records
the arm's bound collector hash, and the identity gates exclude run-identity
fields (acquisition id) while this appendix discloses the concurrency and
amendment history. The analysis code and its unit tests are in
\texttt{experiment/revision/wp1r\_analysis.py}.

\paragraph{Accounting (E4).} Per-request accounting layers
experiment-run $>$ harness-execution $>$ logical-call $>$ provider-attempt;
migration copies are excluded from the totals (distinct re-executions count
individually). Totals: \WpLogicalCalls{} logical calls, \WpHttpAttempts{}
provider attempts, \WpTotalTokens{} known tokens, conservative cost ceiling
\WpCostCny{} CNY at the frozen break-even price of 33.3 CNY per 1M tokens
(pricing not independently verifiable; reported as token counts times the
frozen price, never as billed amounts).

\paragraph{Selector spec (E3).} $\pi_Z$ is multinomial logistic regression
over TF-IDF question features (max 300) and per-member dev accuracies
computed within training folds only; 5-fold task-level CV on the 100 dev
tasks with same-task repeats never split across folds; fold-model
averaging; ties broken by member id; abstain to \bare{} when the top-2
probability gap is below 0.15. Repeat aggregation uses the
available-repeat mean per member--task (same-task repeats stay in one
fold); the final-ledger unknown/failed counts are reconciled against the
merged-matrix NaN cells in the repository checkpoint. Comparators:
\bare{}, dev-fixed, pre-fixed
random member (seeded), M1b (dev-fixed with bare fallback on missing
cells). $E_1$ (budget by construction) is not applicable because panel
members make more than one call; $E_b$ with $b{=}3$ calls per task is
reported as a separately named estimand. Leakage controls: no answer,
correctness, eval-derived difficulty, post-execution trace, or judge
feature is used.

.\REVISION_AUDIT.md:15:> Automatically generated harnesses can differ in source code, execution traces, and correctness outcomes. We study how to interpret these differences on BIRD text-to-SQL with a discovery audit and a post-review reanalysis of an archived factorial study. The discovery audit found outcome-identical pairs and trace-level cases in which declared mechanisms were absent, untriggered, or broken. In the archived factorial study, free ungated generation had 8.56 percentage points of bare-inclusive one-run oracle headroom. The forced-and-gated versus free-and-ungated headroom contrast was -0.16 percentage points (95% CI [-0.83,+0.87]), and the implemented gate excludes two allowed prompt-level strategies. Repeated executions of the same code also produced apparent one-run headroom. These results separate source diversity, executed mechanisms, one-run outcome diversity, stable complementarity, and realized selection utility. They support reporting absolute oracle accuracy, best-fixed accuracy, admission policy, cost, and repeat variability together. They do not establish stable complementarity or a deployable selector. A cost-matched clone control, independent repeats, and frozen held-out selection evaluation remain necessary for that claim.

\begin{abstract}
Automatically generated LLM harnesses offer a rich design space, but their
source-code, execution, and outcome diversity must be measured separately.
On BIRD text-to-SQL, trace inspection distinguishes absent, untriggered,
and broken mechanisms, and free generation yields 8.6\,pp of observed
oracle headroom across 1{,}169 questions; a one-seed MATH-500 probe
shows 10.6\% outcome disagreement and 4.75\,pp headroom. We formalize
one-run oracle gains, stable ranking, stable complementarity,
pre-execution selectability, and budgeted utility as five separately
reported claim classes, checked by ordering-invariance,
dominance-versus-complementarity, cloned-repeat, and condition-mixing
controls with hash-bound challenge re-execution; the procedure also
corrects one of our earlier verification claims. On the archived
factorial study the combined screening intervention estimates
$\RevisionPrimaryDelta$\,pp (95\% CI $\RevisionPrimaryCI$), supporting
the measurement contribution rather than intervention superiority. A
fresh pre-registered MATH-500 collection supplies the decisive
equal-budget control: an eight-harness panel and nine same-code clone
slots, each run for three independent repeats. The panel shows stable
member ranking, but stable complementarity is not established and its
discovery-selected advantage is indistinguishable from same-code
repeated execution. The framework turns apparent diversity into
auditable evidence and identifies the controls required before any
deployment claim.
\end{abstract}

2026-09-15 through 2026-09-19 under a 60{,}000-attempt global budget with
per-cell atomic reservation. Two provider-timeout stops (2026-09-17,
2026-09-18) split the real arm across three continuation ledgers and the
clone arm across two; each continuation re-binds the identical frozen
solver condition (verified field-by-field at merge). The merge rule is
deterministic: a completed observation beats an \texttt{unknown\_remote}
marker; among completed records of the same cell the earliest ledger wins.
Across the real arm's
\WpRowsRead{} rows it collapsed \WpMigrationCopies{} migration
copies, preferred a completed record over an unknown-remote marker
\WpCompletedBeatsUnknown{} times, completed an earlier unknown marker
\WpUnknownThenCompleted{} times, and found \WpDoubleExec{} cells with two
completed but disagreeing executions (first-completed retained; a frozen
sensitivity branch excludes them instead). The clone arm's
\WpCloneRowsRead{} rows collapsed to 10{,}800 unique cells
(\WpCloneMigrationCopies{} copies, zero conflicts).
\WpUnknownCarried{} cells remain
\texttt{unknown\_remote} across all ledgers and stay NaN in the outcome
matrices --- never imputed --- so classes requiring those cells abstain by
the frozen rules. The merged arms are hash-sealed
(\texttt{SEALED\_eval\_real.json}, \texttt{SEALED\_eval\_clone.json},
\texttt{SEALED\_dev\_real.json}). Three collector source versions served
the real arm across continuations (concurrency 2/2/6); each seal records
the arm's bound collector hash, and the identity gates exclude run-identity
fields (acquisition id) while this appendix discloses the concurrency and
amendment history. The analysis code and its unit tests are in
\texttt{experiment/revision/wp1r\_analysis.py}.

\paragraph{Accounting (E4).} Per-request accounting layers
experiment-run $>$ harness-execution $>$ logical-call $>$ provider-attempt;
migration copies are excluded from the totals (distinct re-executions count
individually). Totals: \WpLogicalCalls{} logical calls, \WpHttpAttempts{}
provider attempts, \WpTotalTokens{} known tokens, conservative cost ceiling
\WpCostCny{} CNY at the frozen break-even price of 33.3 CNY per 1M tokens
(pricing not independently verifiable; reported as token counts times the
frozen price, never as billed amounts).

\paragraph{Selector spec (E3).} $\pi_Z$ is multinomial logistic regression
over TF-IDF question features (max 300) and per-member dev accuracies
computed within training folds only; 5-fold task-level CV on the 100 dev
tasks with same-task repeats never split across folds; fold-model
averaging; ties broken by member id; abstain to \bare{} when the top-2
probability gap is below 0.15. Repeat aggregation uses the
available-repeat mean per member--task (same-task repeats stay in one
fold); the final-ledger unknown/failed counts are reconciled against the
merged-matrix NaN cells in the repository checkpoint. Comparators:
\bare{}, dev-fixed, pre-fixed
random member (seeded), M1b (dev-fixed with bare fallback on missing
cells). $E_1$ (budget by construction) is not applicable because panel
members make more than one call; $E_b$ with $b{=}3$ calls per task is
reported as a separately named estimand. Leakage controls: no answer,
correctness, eval-derived difficulty, post-execution trace, or judge
feature is used.

.\REVISION_AUDIT.md:15:> Automatically generated harnesses can differ in source code, execution traces, and correctness outcomes. We study how to interpret these differences on BIRD text-to-SQL with a discovery audit and a post-review reanalysis of an archived factorial study. The discovery audit found outcome-identical pairs and trace-level cases in which declared mechanisms were absent, untriggered, or broken. In the archived factorial study, free ungated generation had 8.56 percentage points of bare-inclusive one-run oracle headroom. The forced-and-gated versus free-and-ungated headroom contrast was -0.16 percentage points (95% CI [-0.83,+0.87]), and the implemented gate excludes two allowed prompt-level strategies. Repeated executions of the same code also produced apparent one-run headroom. These results separate source diversity, executed mechanisms, one-run outcome diversity, stable complementarity, and realized selection utility. They support reporting absolute oracle accuracy, best-fixed accuracy, admission policy, cost, and repeat variability together. They do not establish stable complementarity or a deployable selector. A cost-matched clone control, independent repeats, and frozen held-out selection evaluation remain necessary for that claim.

"""Seal a completed WP-1R arm: verify, snapshot, hash, freeze.

Per protocol section 9/13: SEALED requires every scheduled cell to have a
durable result (success or reconciled unknown/failed), no run_invalid event,
source hashes unchanged since the manifest, and a SHA256-bound snapshot.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WP1R = ROOT / 'artifacts/wp1r_20260915'
EXPECTED = {'eval_real': 10800, 'eval_clone': 10800, 'dev_real': 2700,
           'eval_real_cont': 10800, 'eval_clone_cont': 10800,
           'eval_real_cont2': 10800, 'dev_real_cont2': 2700}


def sha(p: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, 'rb') as f:
        for c in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b''):
            h.update(c)
    return h.hexdigest()


def seal(arm: str) -> dict:
    folder = WP1R / arm
    ledger = folder / 'ledger.sqlite'
    report = {'arm': arm, 'sealed_at': time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime())}
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f'file:{ledger}?mode=ro', uri=True)
    total = conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks').fetchone()[0]
    done = conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE result IS NOT NULL').fetchone()[0]
    report['cells'] = {'total': total, 'with_result': done,
                       'expected': EXPECTED[arm]}
    if total != EXPECTED[arm] or done != total:
        report['state'] = 'NOT_SEALED'
        report['reason'] = 'cells incomplete'
        return report
    invalid = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE json_extract(value,'$.kind')='run_invalid'").fetchone()[0]
    unknown = conn.execute(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE json_extract(result,'$.outcome')='unknown_remote'").fetchone()[0]
    failed = conn.execute(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE json_extract(result,'$.error') IS NOT NULL").fetchone()[0]
    correct = conn.execute(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE json_extract(result,'$.official_correct')=1").fetchone()[0]
    report['cells'].update({'run_invalid': invalid, 'unknown_remote': unknown,
                            'failed': failed, 'official_correct': correct})
    manifest = json.loads(conn.execute('SELECT value FROM manifest WHERE id=1').fetchone()[0])
    # source hashes unchanged since manifest
    drifted = []
    for rel, expected_hash in manifest['source_sha256'].items():
        p = ROOT / rel
        if not p.exists() or sha(p) != expected_hash:
            drifted.append(rel)
    report['source_drift'] = drifted
    counts = {k: v for k, v in report['cells'].items()}
    ok = invalid == 0 and not drifted and counts['failed'] / total <= 0.15
    report['state'] = 'SEALED' if ok else 'NOT_SEALED'
    if report['state'] == 'SEALED':
        snap = {
            'arm': arm, 'sealed_at': report['sealed_at'],
            'manifest': manifest,
            'cells': report['cells'],
            'ledger_sha256': sha(ledger),
        }
        (folder / 'SEALED.json').write_text(json.dumps(snap, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False),
                                            encoding='utf-8')
    return report


def seal_merged(arm: str) -> dict:
    """Seal a merged arm across its continuation ledgers (post-2026-09-17).

    The stop-and-reconcile events split each arm across ledgers; the
    meaningful completeness statement is over the merged unique-cell view
    produced by the deterministic precedence rule of wp1r_analysis.
    """
    from experiment.revision.wp1r_analysis import ARM_LEDGERS, merge_cells
    names = [n for n in ARM_LEDGERS[arm]
             if (WP1R / n / 'ledger.sqlite').exists()]
    cell_map, dedup = merge_cells(names)
    invalid = 0
    ledger_hashes = {}
    for n in names:
        ledger = WP1R / n / 'ledger.sqlite'
        conn = sqlite3.connect(f'file:{ledger}?mode=ro', uri=True)
        invalid += conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events "
            "WHERE json_extract(value,'$.kind')='run_invalid'").fetchone()[0]
        conn.close()
        ledger_hashes[n] = sha(ledger)
    unknown = sum(1 for c in cell_map.values()
                  if c.get('official_correct') is None)
    # source drift: measured sources (harnesses, split, runtime, bridge)
    # must be byte-frozen across ledgers AND match the working tree; the
    # collector itself legitimately evolved across continuation boundaries
    # (race fix dd5a773, concurrency amendments) and each ledger binds the
    # bytes it was created with -- recorded as provenance, not a failure.
    collector = 'experiment\\revision\\fresh_collect_math.py'
    manifests = []
    for n in names:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(
            f"file:{WP1R / n / 'ledger.sqlite'}?mode=ro", uri=True)
        manifests.append(json.loads(conn.execute(
            'SELECT value FROM manifest WHERE id=1').fetchone()[0]))
        conn.close()
    drifted = []
    for rel, expected_hash in manifests[0]['source_sha256'].items():
        if rel.replace('/', '\\') == collector or rel == collector:
            continue
        p = ROOT / rel
        if not p.exists() or sha(p) != expected_hash:
            drifted.append(rel)
        for m in manifests[1:]:
            if m['source_sha256'].get(rel) != expected_hash:
                drifted.append(f'{rel} (cross-ledger)')
    collector_versions = sorted({
        m['source_sha256'].get(collector) or
